reflection.quote: It is not the mountain we conquer, but ourselves.
reflection.reading:
The last Monday of August has a particular weight to it. Summer is thinning out, the light shifts earlier, and there's this quiet pressure to have gotten something out of the past few months — a tan, a trip, a story. When I was drinking, this week used to gut me. I'd look back at a summer I couldn't remember and feel the year slipping through my hands. Another season spent as a passenger in my own life.

Sobriety didn't hand me a spectacular summer by default. What it handed me was the raw material — mornings I actually woke up for, weekends I remember, the ability to say yes to a hike or a road trip and actually show up. What I did with that material was on me. Some summers I've filled with big things: a ski season, a jump out of a plane, a hunt with people I love. Other summers were quieter — coffee on the porch, a book finished, dinners with friends. Both counted. Both were mine.

Hillary wasn't talking about mountains, not really. The thing you build in getting sober isn't a highlight reel. It's the person underneath — the one who can be counted on, who can sit in an ordinary Monday and not need to escape it. That's the summit worth reaching. And you reach it one plain day at a time.
reflection.meditation: Sit for a moment with the summer behind you. Not the version you wish you'd had — the one that actually happened. What did you show up for? Who did you get to be, because you were present for it?

affirmations: I am the person my summer was built around, not a passenger in it.
Today I show up for the ordinary hours, because that's where my life actually happens.
I am building someone I can live with, one plain day at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful today for a summer I can actually remember — the loud parts and the quiet ones. Grateful for the friends who saw me sober, for mornings that started clear, for the ability to close out August without dread about what I did or didn't do. The gift was never a perfect season. The gift was being awake for it.
gratitude.closing: One more day, one more Monday, both feet on the ground.
